testCase.name: [local] S08 Web browser with the wrong date and time zone shows the same day/visit number, badge, 'New today' and DOB age

descriptionHtml:
Case priority: P0 · stated in the UAT / ticket AC · TFA-92579 AC 4; UAT 3.8 · “A phone with a wrong clock, no clock set, or a different time zone shows the same state”. Mixed: stated part — day/visit number and badge identical with a wrong browser date and time zone; our part — age from DOB on a birthday boundary, the 'New today' chip (only the stated part makes a QA bug).

Bug B18 · S1 · known

Many dates and times follow the device clock instead of server time (UAT 3.8): 'NEW TODAY', admit date, vitals date, task done time, transcript date; with a phone two days slow a held drug is stamped two days back and the next cleanup deletes it

Tickets: TFA-92584 ready for qa (UAT 3.8); TFA-92597 ready for qa (R6); TFA-92579 AC 3/4 ready for qa (NEW TODAY); TFA-94745 ready for qa (draft restore) · counts as a QA bug: yes · found on: local

Note: Root cause known (Daniela asked for server time on 10-03); the deleted drug, missing badge and wrong draft restore are new symptoms. TC-16/S18 (UAT 3.8, one device set to the wrong date): a phone a day ahead files its bedside line in a row dated tomorrow on the shared record, and the next write from a correctly clocked device lists the lines before it twice (the transcript archive trusts the device date). Which calendar day a correct device should use when its local day and the server's UTC day differ is the open question Q9 (D10); TC-16/S25 passed otherwise. Review 2026-10-14 (TFA-92579/92584): a browser whose day is ahead writes the badge roll back to the server, and every device shows Follow-up, with the matching template and billing family (TC-01/S08, TC-20/S20a; TFA-92584 AC 8). The failing cell of TC-25/S24a is the card's NEW TODAY, which compares addedAt with the device's date (PatientCard.tsx:154-156). EFS/S28 (a)(b) restore drafts by the device date (TFA-94745); (c), an old draft put in today's box, is B13's. Review 2026-10-15 (TFA-94514): the analytics day is the device date too (pilotUsageEvents / pilotDailyRounding use localDay()): a phone 3 days ahead files its rows under its own day, and an encounter across the phone midnight is split over two days and never timed (OAT-06/S10). Re-test 2026-10-16 (TC-21/S26, 25acd727): a browser two days ahead writes the badge roll with its own future day (encTypeDay 2026-10-19) to the shared record, so the correct-clock browser shows Follow-up too. Re-test 2026-10-20 on 8b4be94a: changed: task done time and Important Points now use server time (TC-22/S23, TC-12/S23, TC-07/S28 stamp); still device time: Tomorrow's Pre-Round Summary edit (TC-17/S25), task screen header date (TC-07/S28), handoff title date (TC-08/S20), medicationsUpdatedAt (TC-19/S19), NEW TODAY (TC-01/S08), completeEncounter day (OAT-06/S10).

Other cases of the same bug (counted once): TC-10/S22, TC-12/S23, TC-19/S19, TC-22/S23, TC-25/S24a, TC-02/S13b, EFS/S28, TC-16/S18, TC-06/S19, OAT-06/S10, TC-06/S23, TC-21/S22, TC-25/S24b, TC-19/S23, TC-21/S26, TC-17/S25, TC-07/S28, TC-08/S20

Approach · TC-01 Patient Chart Card · S08 Web browser with the wrong date and time zone shows the same day/visit number, badge, 'New today' and DOB age

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U6 The day/visit number advances each calendar day by server time and never stays frozen; a device with a wrong clock or time zone shows the same number. (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 4; UAT 3.8)
  • U4 The card shows the New Admission / Follow-up / Consult badge. (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 3)
  • U3 The card shows age/sex in the "76F" format. (UAT TC-01; TFA-92579 AC 3)

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given Same account and seededCensus in two Playwright browser contexts: A normal; B with timezoneId 'Pacific/Honolulu' and page.clock.setSystemTime(server now + 1 d)

When Open the Hospital list and both Nursing Home lists in A and in B

Then For every card the day/visit number, the badge and the presence of 'New today' are identical in A and B; N6 (87th birthday today by server date) shows 87 and N7 (birthday tomorrow) shows 86 in both contexts

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): UAT 3.8: identical state on both clocks; per card, compare A and B (card-scoped locators 'Open chart for <name>'). knownGaps: the badge mismatch only, 'TFA-92584 AC 8' (main computes the badge with localDay()). A day/visit number or 'New today' mismatch (main's 'New today' uses new Date()) reports against TFA-92579 AC 3/4. DOB rows: 87 / 86 in both contexts under Q12; …

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S08 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-01.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Triage (2026-10-14): 1 row.

Issue type: New product issue · environment local · tickets TFA-92579 ready for qa; TFA-92584 ready for qa

On a computer whose clock or time zone is a day off, a patient added today does not get the 'NEW TODAY' tag that every other device shows, and opening the list on that computer also flips New Admission and Consult badges to Follow-up for every device.

Evidence: newspec-a (final2 run). Browsers B (Honolulu, +1 d) and B2 (UTC, +1 d) both lose 'NEW TODAY' on H3/HX, because PatientCard compares addedAt with the device date. This was only predicted in the TC-01 risks; it is not in the dev report or ledger, and the matrix sends it to TFA-92579 AC 3/4 as not known. The badge roll is known (TFA-92584 AC 8, device-clock localDay). DOB ages are recorded only (Q12). Day/visit numbers are missing in every context (see S06/S26).

Environment: local — main e02167f → 8b4be94a (10-20), local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script; secondary: MULTI · Multi-device / multi-account — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.
